The '''2019–20 New Zealand Football Championship''' season (currently known as the '''ISPS Handa Premiership''' for sponsorship reasons) was the sixteenth season of the NZFC since its establishment, in 2004. Ten teams compete in the competition with [[Eastern Suburbs AFC|Eastern Suburbs]] and [[Auckland City FC|Auckland City]] representing the ISPS Handa Premiership in the [[2020 OFC Champions League]] after finishing Champions (Eastern Suburbs) and Premiers (Auckland City) respectively in the [[2018–19 New Zealand Football Championship|2018–19]] competition.

==Regular season==

===League table===
On 18 March 2020, [[New Zealand Football]] announced that the 2019–20 New Zealand Football Championship season had been concluded due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The remaining two rounds of the regular season and the finals series were cancelled. [[Auckland City FC|Auckland City]], who were leading the regular season table, were declared champions and also awarded the Minor Premiership, and qualified for the [[2021 OFC Champions League]] together with [[Team Wellington FC|Team Wellington]], who were at second place in the regular season table.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/88417?newsfeedId=634683|title=Premiership concluded, Auckland City champions|publisher=New Zealand Football|date=18 March 2020|access-date=20 March 2020|archive-date=4 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200604224353/https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/88417?newsfeedId=634683|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aucklandcityfc.com/news/1174/12/Auckland-City-FC-declared-champions-/|title=Auckland City FC declared champions|publisher=Auckland City FC|date=18 March 2020}}</ref>

===Fixtures and results===
The season was scheduled to be played on a home and away basis between November 2019 and March 2020, with the finals series being played in April 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Draw released for ISPS Handa Premiership |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/82584 |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |accessdate=27 September 2019 |archive-date=11 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200911175612/https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/82584 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
